AfterCombatEnd.rationale: PaelsFlesh.cs:86-91 resets base.Status and refreshes the display. Presentation only; there is no mechanical field to reset (contrast paels_tears and paels_legion in this batch, whose AfterCombatEnd clears real state and whose ports are gaps for dropping it).

guards.what: N1: `player.PlayerCombatState.TurnNumber < 3` (PaelsFlesh.cs:43) vs the sim's `self.turn < self.FROM_TURN` (paels_flesh.py:24) -- are the two counters the same number, including across EXTRA turns?
guards.rationale: Verified at the source rather than assumed, because C# deliberately distinguishes PlayerCombatState.TurnNumber from ICombatState.RoundNumber (ICombatState.cs:56 'BE CAREFUL!') and this relic reads the former. TurnNumber initialises to 1 (PlayerCombatState.cs:37) and is bumped by IncrementTurnNumber (:157-159), called from CombatManager.SwitchSides (CombatManager.cs:1415-1418) on BOTH the enemy->player switch and the player->player extra-turn switch -- and RoundNumber (:1413) only on the former. The sim's combat.turn starts at 1 (combat.py:108) and is incremented in both of end_turn's paths, the extra turn at combat.py:650 and the normal one at :674, in each case BEFORE player.start_turn() -- so the energy reset for turn N reads N on both sides, and an extra turn advances the relic's gate on both sides. Executed cross-check: `py audit/tools/relic_probes.py turn-order` shows on_energy_reset(turn=2) after the first end_turn, i.e. the increment precedes the reset.

Structurally satisfied: hooks.py:207 passes the combat's single PlayerCombatState, and player.py:163 is the only caller of the dispatcher. Multiplayer-only parameter check, noted per the shared contract rather than verdicted as a divergence.
